title: Proposal quality and the proposer prompt: what the 49 v3 proposals were, why they died, and a tested per-code conditional proposer for v5
verdict_cn:
结论：改进“出规则”这一步的提示词，技术上容易，也便宜；但没有证据表明它能让规则真正被接受。

我做了什么：逐条读了上一轮（第三版）的49条候选规则。其中21条在正式测试前就被淘汰，大多死于格式和流程的小毛病：8条因为引用的4到6道例题里有1道错误类型不对，整条作废；8条因为同类错题太少，没法测；还有3次整份回复因为某一栏超出字数限制4到21个字而全部重问，白花了约19万个计费单位（token）。两名评审（我和另一个模型）都认为，49条里只有7条是真正的新建议，其余多在重复或细化原有的任务说明。约一半是“所有题都适用”的笼统要求。15条互相矛盾，例如一条要“答案越短越好”，另一条要“写全名”。

新写法：每类错误单独问一次，同时给出“错在反方向的题”和“本来就做对的题”，并要求规则写成“当……时，做……；否则……”。我用GLM（项目里负责出规则的那个大模型）在第一阶段问答题上试了。7条规则全部带条件，没有一条泄露答案。最好的一条只作用于97道题中的14道，覆盖全部5道目标错题，只碰到72道做对题中的3道。同样的题用旧写法，出了1条笼统规则，另有2条泄露答案。

但旧规则失败的主因是效果太小，淹没在随机波动里，提示词改不了这一点。建议下一版采用新写法，但不要把它当作方法有效的证据。
what_i_did:
1) Traced all 49 v3 proposals (I-ds/E-ds, s1-s5) from the raw analyst reply through prepare, selftest, screen and confirm (trace.py over prepare/selftest/screen/confirm unit.json, prepare/attempt-1/roles.json and research.json). Funnel reproduced: 49 -> 28 supported -> 15 screened -> 2 confirmed -> 0 accepted. The context file's "14 screened" is a typo; its own later line counts 15.
2) Rebuilt all 10 analyst payloads with the frozen v3 code. The recorded request SHA-256 matched 10 of 10.
3) Measured every raw reply field against its limit, to explain the 3 whole-reply rejections and the 1 invalid row.
4) Re-ran the frozen v3 mechanical leakage checks on all 49 texts and on every selftest revision.
5) Analysed the 8 evidence-invalid rules and counted, per code, the failed items in each half.
6) Coded all 49 by hand (14 clusters; global/conditional form; restatement of the card or seed; contradictions). Got an independent GLM-5.3 second rating (one call per benchmark) and computed agreement (kappa).
7) Verified that the cal-1 arm file matches the old machine (md5 equal). Its cand arm is v3 E-ds s1-r1, and its seed-rule arm is the seed bullet that rule restates.
8) Read analyst.py (ANALYST_SYSTEM, payload, evidence_problem, _transfer, _row), step.py (prepare, _admissible, trigger), leakage.py, protocol.py, roles.py and skill.py.
9) Drafted the v5 per-code conditional proposer prompt and piloted it with GLM-5.3 on E-ds s1 SearchQA training data (proposal half only): D1 twice, D2 once plus a re-ask carrying its validation errors, the v3 prompt on the same D1 items as an ablation, and a GLM applicability judge over the 99-item check half. Validated every reply (limits, evidence ids, frozen leakage checks, trigger sizes against MIN_TRIGGER). Wrote the full report.
evidence:
All measured unless marked. Prepare-stage deaths: 21 of 49 (43%).
- 8 evidence_invalid, all evidence_other_code. Each had exactly 1 off-code citation among 4-6, and only 1 of those 8 items carried the targeted code on another run.
- 8 insufficient_support (trigger 0-3, below 4). Triggers are defined by the code, not the rule; all 8 codes had fewer than 4 failed check-half items.
- 4 leakage drops: I-ds s1-r5 answer_text, I-ds s3-r1 option_text (it quotes the meta-option sentence), I-ds s1-r3 adjudicated (its example "Minsk, Monrovia, Manama" gives an answer away), E-ds s3-r1 adjudicated (meta-option mapping).
- 1 invalid row: adds field 304 of 300 characters.
Later deaths: selftest 13 (10 after revision, 3 not revised; E-ds s2-r4's revision leaked the OfficeQA reference number 4.815), screen 13 (all C1), confirm 2 (1 C1, 1 C2 with rest delta -15/2).
Whole-reply rejections: 3 of 13 analyst calls. Two had transfer.none at 307 and 321 of 300 characters; one had every row missing placement (ALFWorld). Wasted: 187,425 of 749,469 analyst tokens (25%).
Transfer slot: 2 replies named a local rule (silent void); 1 similar-placement rule in 49, dead at insufficient_support.
Form (me / GLM): global-ish 28/26 of 49, kappa 0.67 for global vs conditional. Restatement of the seed or card: 8 by both raters, 18 by me. New advice: 7 by both raters. A lexical-overlap proxy failed to separate these classes (0.21 vs 0.18).
Contradictions: 15 of 49 proposals involved. Within-reply pairs appear in 5 of 10 replies, each pair built on opposite-direction taxonomy codes; in 4 of the 5 pairs one side died at prepare.
Screened rules by form: conditional n=5, mean gain 0.50 items; global n=6, mean 0.04; quasi-conditional n=4, mean 0.00. Not distinguishable at the noise floor.
Pilot, v5 prompt: 7 of 7 final rules conditional; 5 of 7 within every limit; 0 of 7 leakage findings.
Pilot, v3-prompt ablation on the same items: 5 rules, 1 global, 2 with leakage hits (answer_word licorice/lingual; answer_text). One cites the Forbes-magazine item but steers to "Forbes", the wrong direction. The transfer void recurred.
Applicability (GLM judge, 97 judged check-half items: 25 failing, 72 always correct):
- best condition ("your candidate shares a content word with the question"): applies to 14 items, 11 of them failing, D1 recall 5/5, 3 of 72 always-correct items exposed;
- the "this <category>" condition: applies to 49 of 97, so effectively global;
- judge-based MIN_TRIGGER passes for 5 of 7 conditions (two have 0 and 3 failing items, although v3's code-based trigger would have passed them).
Self-labels vs judge: fixes 19/26, spares 17/22. Re-ask with errors fixed 2 of 5 problems; length went from 917 to 709 characters, still over 600. Stability across two runs: the same 3 themes, different text.

pilot.command: ssh -o BatchMode=yes <datatools-login> "bash -ic 'proxy_on >/dev/null 2>&1; cd /data/feasibility/D13/run2/scripts && P=/root/continual-alf-prep-20260928/env/bin/python; $P -I pilot.py build D1 D2; $P -I pilot.py build D2 D1; $P -I pilot.py call D1 a; $P -I pilot.py call D1 b; $P -I pilot.py call D2 a; $P -I followup.py reask D2 \"$(cat ../out/D2_errors.json)\"; $P -I followup.py v3abl; $P -I check.py ../out/pilot_reply_D1_a.json ../out/pilot_reply_D1_b.json ../out/pilot_reply_D2_a.json ../out/pilot_reply_D2_reask.json; $P -I check_v3abl.py; $P -I judge.py; $P -I trig.py; $P -I rater.py'"
pilot.result: GLM-5.3 (temperature 0, max_tokens 16384, the v3 role settings) on E-ds s1 SearchQA training data, proposal half. D1 call: 95,433 bytes (12 D1 items, 4 D2, 6 always correct). D2 call: 74,134 bytes. Seven final rules (3 per D1 run, 1 D2 after its re-ask), all conditional with a default. Five of 7 are within every limit and 0 of 7 have a frozen-v3 leakage finding. Best rule (D1 run b): 'When your candidate answer contains a content word that also appears verbatim in the question itself ...: delete that repeated word ...; Otherwise, keep the candidate as is'. It applies to 14 of 97 judged check-half items, 11 of them failing, with D1 recall 5/5 and 3 of 72 always-correct items exposed. The 'this <category>' rule applies to 49 of 97 (effectively global). The D1 and D2 rules were mutually consistent: drop words the question supplies; add a qualifier only when the question lacks it and the snippets repeat it. v3 had contradicted itself here, but this is one pair only. The D2 rule broke the length limits, and one re-ask with the errors still left it at 709 of 600 characters. v3-prompt ablation on the same items: 1 global rule of 5, 2 with leakage hits, 1 steering in the wrong direction, and the transfer slot voided again. Judge-based MIN_TRIGGER passes for 5 of 7 conditions. No solver run was made, so no claim is made about fixes or score gains.

risks:
- The applicability judge is a single GLM pass on question plus parent draft, without snippets. It agreed with the proposer's self-labels only about 75%; it needs reason-then-label, 3 votes and a 20-item audit.
- Draft-dependent conditions are judged on the parent's draft; the rule arm's draft may differ.
- About 2.7x more proposer calls and more candidate rules raise multiplicity at screen (D8). Cap rules at 2 per code and 5 per stage after a cross-code consistency check.
- Per-code calls can still contradict each other across codes; the pilot's consistent pair is n=1.
- Temperature-0 GLM is not deterministic: the same themes come back with different texts, and the best rule appeared in only one of two runs.
- One generic re-ask does not fix over-long compound conditions.
- The LiveMath meta-option conflict between the taxonomy and option-text leakage is a policy issue (D7); the prompt cannot fix it.
- Some SearchQA D1 failures are reference truncations that no observable condition predicts.
- The restatement coding is subjective (4-way kappa 0.41). The robust claim is "8 restatements by both raters, 18 by one".
- The main risk is over-reading: better proposals are not evidence of a method effect. C1 (14 of 15 screened) is a noise and headroom limit.
